course_description:
This course builds on the foundation service management course and examines service management theory in the context of the world's best hospitality and service organisations to better understand service excellence, service orientation and service culture. The course examines leadership at two levels - the individual level (people as leaders) and the organisational level (companies as leaders). Topics include the study of leadership theories and styles, creating a service-oriented organisational culture and values, decision-making, team dynamics, the role of emotions in leadership, and a review of international best practice hospitality organisations. Students will study industry best practice and create their own comprehensive case studies of service excellence in hospitality.

Through the study of leadership theory, an advanced interrogation of critical leadership issues affecting the service sector broadly, numerous leadership self-appraisals, and the integration of a number of invited speakers from industry,ﾠstudents will be exposed to a blend of leadership theories, service leadership practices and leadership self evaluations.

Sustainable Development Goal s - UQ Business School is a proud supporter and Advanced Signatory of the United Nations Principles for Responsible Management Education (UN PRME) . As part of the largest global collaboration between business schools and the UN, the school emphasises its role in empowering students to drive societal transformation through the Sustainable Development Goals . The SDGs highlight that a thriving economy relies on a healthy environment, aiming to balance economic growth, social well-being, and environmental protection for a sustainable future.

course_aims: This course aims to provide students with a deep understanding about leadership and leading service organisations. The course focuses long term and more strategically than the core "service management" course. It seeks to gain a greater understanding about how hospitality organisations can first set organisational aims, mission and vision, and then how to put the activities and actions required in to place to fulfil organisational aspirations. Leadership is explored from both a personal and organisational perspective.

learning_outcomes.description: Critically evaluate leadership theories, styles and philosophies in a service and hospitality context.
Self-evaluate your leadership style to effectively utilise personal strengths and beliefs in leading people and service organisations.
Consider the importance of long term focus, and how to align hospitality organisational aims, mission, vision, values and strategies.
Analyse hospitality businesses in order to identify critical leadership success factors.

assessment_details.title: Leadership Compass & Team Inventory Analysis
assessment_details.task_description: Students will use the Leadership Compass and the Team Inventory Tools provided to evaluate their own leadership traits, skills and values in a 1000 word reflection. First, use the Leadership Compass to evaluate your own leadership traits, skills and values. The result of the Leadership Compass will provide a dominant leadership perspective. Second, complete the Team Inventory to determine your preferences in working with others and making decisions when working in teams. Once these tools have provided you with results. You will write up a personal reflection that shares your results and an analysis of how, where and when these results have been present in your academic, professional or personal life. assessment_details.title: Leadership Analysis and Self-Evaluation
assessment_details.task_description: This is an individual, 2,500 word report in which you analyse and evaluate your own leadership practice in a service context. Rather than simply labelling yourself with one leadership ‘style’, you will examine how you actually lead, the various approaches you draw on, and evaluate your leadership across three connected dimensions: your own development as a leader, your impact on others and teams, and your ethical responsibilities. Throughout, situate your analysis in the service and hospitality context: your leadership shapes the employee experience, which in turn shapes the guest experience (e.g. the service-profit chain). assessment_details.task_description: This is a problem-based assessment whereby students will have to apply service leadership principles, theories and approaches to address real-world situations and challenges facing all service industries - with a focus on the tourism, hospitality and events sectors. The assessment will assess your understanding of the content from all modules we have covered this semester. This is a 2 hour exam paper with 10 minutes reading time. The format of the assessment includes short answer questions in which you will be asked to apply concepts covered this semester to solve various service leadership problems and scenarios. More details will be provided in class, as well as preparation advice. Criteria & Marking: Further information will be provided on Blackboard and in class. learning_activities.topic: Course Introduction / Linking Leadership to the Service and Hospitality Context Leadership vs management; the hospitality leadership context; the experience economy; moments of truth and frontline discretion; the service-profit chain introduced as the course spine; bridging from service management to leadership. Learning outcomes: L01, L04

Leadership Identity and Self-Awareness Leadership identity and self-concept; personal values and values clarification; strengths-based leadership; self-awareness and reflective practice; the Leadership Compass as a diagnostic of your dominant perspective. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Leading with Others: Team Roles and Followership Team dynamics and team roles; followership and why people choose to follow; collaboration, conflict styles and working across differences; the Team Inventory as a diagnostic; interdependence in frontline service teams. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04

Trait, Behavioural and Skills Approaches Trait, behavioural and skills approaches to leadership; technical, human and conceptual skills; strengths and limitations of leader-centred theories; applying these lenses to interpret your Compass and Team Inventory results. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04

Situational and Adaptive Leadership Contingency thinking and matching style to context; situational leadership and follower readiness; adaptive leadership (technical vs adaptive challenges); leadership flexibility; flexing to guests, staff and shifting demand. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04

Transformational and Authentic Leadership Transformational leadership and the four I's; vision, empowerment and motivation; authentic leadership and trust; transactional vs transformational; inspiring discretionary effort in a guest-facing culture. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Emotional Intelligence and Leadership Emotional intelligence and Goleman's dimensions; emotional labour (surface vs deep acting); empathy and reading the guest; communication, feedback and difficult conversations; the satisfaction mirror; technostress and AI on the frontline. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04

Building and Leading Service Culture with a Service-Profit Chain Lens Organisational culture; trust, psychological safety, employee engagement and discretionary effort; servant leadership and internal service quality — culture as the engine of the chain; leadership ethics in service — the leader's responsibilities to employees and guests, fairness and respect (introducing the ethical lens assessed in Assessment 2). Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04

Strategic Leadership Strategic thinking and vision; organisational purpose, mission, vision and values; aligning people, performance and purpose with a long-term focus; stakeholder management and responsibilities, and the consequences of strategic decisions (extending the ethical lens for Assessment 2). Learning outcomes: L03, L04

Assessment 2 Workshop Intensive workshopping of Assessment 2; interpreting your leadership practice through the literature and a personal experience; coaching on the relational and ethical evaluation criteria and your development plan; peer feedback and collaborative support. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Leading Change and Innovation Change leadership and resistance to change; innovation and experimentation; digital transformation and AI in hospitality; the reimagined service-profit chain (support-AI and experience-AI); leading people through disruption. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Leadership in Crisis and Uncertainty Crisis leadership and leading under pressure; resilience and trust under pressure; decision-making and sensemaking in uncertainty; communication during crisis; the "repair" dimension of service recovery; hospitality's exposure to external shocks. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

The Future Leader The future of work and changing workforce expectations; sustainability and responsible leadership; leadership capabilities for the next decade; synthesis — revisiting the service-profit chain end-to-end and rewriting your leadership definition; does "unreasonable hospitality" scale? / Exam review and Course final remarks Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
